label: Pérez-Mañá 2022
threshold: cut-off score of 105 or 106 (paper does not state direction; lower score = lower QoL = visual impairment, so score at or below cut-off = positive)
ref_threshold: Visual impairment group: best-corrected distance visual acuity in the best eye equal or inferior to 0.30 logMAR (public hospital) or 0.52 logMAR (private clinic); healthy group: best-corrected distance VA equal or superior to 0.10 logMAR in the worst eye (p2)
derivation: n = 170 + 195 (VI + healthy, p4); n_positive = 170; prevalence = 170/365; sens/spec as 95.4%/91.8% (p4). TP/FP/FN/TN left blank: 95.4% is not reproduced by any TP/170 (162/170=95.3, 163/170=95.9), spec 0.918 matches 179/195; denominators for ROC not stated (pitfall 10)
notes: Case-control (VI vs healthy) ROC; paper says cut-off 105 or 106 optimal, one row recorded; single ROC area not reported; ref_threshold_logmar 0.3 is the public-hospital cut, private clinic used 0.52; "equal or inferior to 0.30" is ambiguous in direction (Table 2 p5 shows VI public range 0.3 to 2, so worse than or equal to 0.3); authors warn of over-estimation from clear-cut cases/controls (p9); sample for ROC assumed to be all 365
